items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: he would add Billy Butterfield on trumpet and Peanut Hucko on clarinet or tenor

ctx.x: black, and I felt I was always accepted by them as an equal -- not just a pretty good white drummer.

And oh yes, by the same token, I've worked with some black musicians with big reputations, who didn't have time and music in his bones, a statement I make with tongue in cheek -- some didn't swing worth a bleep, and played unmercifully out of tune and with bad taste, and on the other hand, some of the great white musicians I played with could never be surpassed for greatness -- black, blue, green or otherwise. Jack Teagarden, Lou McGarity, Billy Butterfield, Venus Huckie, Joe Vanuti, Dave McKenner, Bob Haggard on…
I'll sum up by saying it about evens out. To me, God passed out the talent in this world in a dimly lit room.
